title: The United Nations
examples: What is the main job of the United Nations?
Can you explain the role of the Security Council?
Which UN agency deals with health issues?

explain.say: The United Nations is a big group of countries working together.
It tries to solve big world problems peacefully.
The Security Council is a key part that keeps peace.
It can recommend actions when there is a serious threat.
The UN has many specialized agencies for specific needs.
When a country faces a health crisis, the WHO helps coordinate aid.

faq.q: What is the main goal of the United Nations?
faq.a: Its main goal is to promote international cooperation and maintain global peace and security. It helps countries work together to solve big problems.
asks: What does the UN try to achieve?

faq.q: Who has the power to make decisions in the Security Council?
faq.a: The Security Council has fifteen members, including five permanent members with veto power. This means some countries have more say than others.
asks: Does every country have an equal vote?
How does the Security Council vote?

faq.q: What is the difference between the UN and a local government?
faq.a: The UN deals with issues between entire sovereign nations. Local governments handle things within one specific city or region.
asks: Is the UN like a world parliament?
Does the UN make laws for everyone?

faq.q: Can the UN force countries to change their laws?
faq.a: The UN can pass resolutions, which are strong recommendations. However, enforcing these resolutions often requires the agreement of member states.

faq.q: What kind of problems do the UN agencies handle?
faq.a: Agencies handle specific areas like health, education, or child welfare. For example, UNICEF focuses only on children's rights.
asks: Are there UN agencies for everything?

facts: The UN was established after the Second World War.
It has many member states representing almost every country on Earth.
The Security Council is one of the main organs of the UN.
Agencies like WHO focus on specific global challenges.

quiz.say: The UN's primary focus is to:

options.show: Pass laws only for developed countries.
options.say: Pass laws only for developed countries.

quiz.why: This is the core mandate given to the organization by its founding members.

wrong.1: The UN does not have the power to manage the economies of independent nations.
wrong.2: The UN works with existing national governments, it does not replace them.
wrong.3: Its principles apply to all member states regardless of their economic status.

quiz.say: If a region has a major outbreak of disease, which agency is most likely to help?
quiz.why: WHO is the specialized agency dedicated to global public health issues.

wrong.0: The Security Council deals with political threats, not medical outbreaks.
wrong.1: UNESCO focuses on culture and education, not immediate health emergencies.
wrong.2: While UNICEF helps children, WHO is the main health authority.

quiz.say: A country wants to establish a global standard for clean water access. Which UN body would be most involved in setting guidelines?

options.show: A relevant specialized agency or committee.
options.say: A relevant specialized agency or committee.

options.show: Voting directly through the General Assembly.
options.say: Voting directly through the General Assembly.

options.show: A single member nation deciding alone.
options.say: A single member nation deciding alone.

quiz.why: These agencies are experts in specific fields and create detailed guidelines for member states.

wrong.1: The Security Council handles threats to peace, not technical standards like water quality.
wrong.2: While the General Assembly discusses it, the experts in an agency create the technical standard.
wrong.3: The UN requires international consensus to set global standards.
